question.text:
A polynomial p with rational coefficients satisfies p(e) = p(1). What must p(2) − p(1) equal?
2
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) e − 1 (D) e − 1 (E) It is not determined.

solution.text:
The rational-coefficient polynomial q(x) = p(x) − p(1) vanishes at the transcendental
number e. If it were nonzero, multiplying by a common denominator would give a nonzero
integer-coefficient polynomial with root e, a contradiction. Thus q is identically zero and p
is constant.

5x 2x
Subtract the two derivative quotients (e − 1)/x and (e − 1)/x. Their limits are 5 and 2,
giving 3.

question.text:
For which real c does log x ≤ c(x − 1) hold for every x > 0?
(A) c ≥ 1 (B) c ≤ 1 (C) c = 1 only (D) c > 0 (E) No such c

solution.text:
For x > 1, dividing by x − 1 and letting x ↓ 1 forces c ≥ 1. For 0 < x < 1, division reverses
the inequality and x ↑ 1 forces c ≤ 1. The value c = 1 works because x − 1 − log x has
derivative 1 − 1/x, decreases to zero at 1, and then increases.
